marketBlock.demoExplainer: <lead>The price on this market is set by hand by the operator.</lead> The contracts, the staking and the settlement are the real ones — only the feed is not. It exists because a round cannot resolve until its feed publishes after the close, and a real feed’s heartbeat runs to tens of minutes; here a round can be watched all the way through.

terms.heading: Terms
terms.unavailable: The contract terms are unavailable right now.

staking.title: Staking
staking.yieldRateNote: Simple, not compounding — yield never folds back into the earning base, so what you earn is a function of stake and time and nothing else.
staking.withdrawalsNote: Staking is not locked. A withdrawal is limited only by what your debt allows: enough collateral has to stay to keep the position above the liquidation threshold.

borrowing.title: Borrowing
borrowing.maxLtvNote: The most you may borrow against your stake. A borrow that would cross this is refused rather than allowed and then liquidated.
borrowing.thresholdNote: Where the health factor reaches 1.00 and liquidation becomes possible.
borrowing.thresholdNoteGap: Where the health factor reaches 1.00 and liquidation becomes possible. The gap above the LTV ceiling is deliberate: it is the room a position has to accrue interest before anyone can touch it.
borrowing.kinkNote: Where the borrow rate stops rising gently and starts rising steeply, so lenders are paid to refill a pool that is running dry.

liquidated.title: If you are liquidated
liquidated.closeFactorNote: The most of your debt one liquidation may clear. It caps what a single price dip costs you — the rest of the position survives it.
liquidated.bonusNote: The discount a liquidator takes on the collateral they seize, paid out of your position. It is what makes anyone show up to close an underwater loan, which is what keeps the pool solvent.
liquidated.fullNote: Below this health factor the close-factor cap is lifted and the whole lien may be cleared at once. It is derived on chain from the threshold and the bonus, not configured — it is precisely the point where a capped liquidation stops making a position healthier.

rounds.title: Taking a position
rounds.intro: Odds come from how the pool splits, so the protocol never takes the other side of your view.
rounds.rakeNote: Taken from the losing pool at settlement, so it is already inside the odds you were shown rather than deducted from a win afterwards.
rounds.entryCutoffNote: Entry closes before the round locks so nobody can take a side in the last second against a price they can already see moving.
rounds.minimumPerSideNote: A round whose losing side never reaches this is voided and every stake is refunded in full — a one-sided pool has nothing to pay a winner from.

fees.heading: Protocol earnings
fees.rakeNote: Taken from the losing pool at settlement. A voided round takes none at all — rake is only recorded on the resolve path — so a market on a slow feed earns nothing while it is voiding.
fees.rakeBound: Capped by the rake collected, not by the token balance, so this cannot reach stakes still owed to users — including a resolved round's unclaimed winnings.
fees.reservesNote: The protocol's cut of borrower interest, credited when interest accrues into the index rather than when a borrower pays.
fees.reservesBound: Subordinated to suppliers: a withdrawal is refused unless the pool still holds enough cash to meet every supplier claim afterwards. Credited interest that nobody has paid is not withdrawable.
fees.predatesTreasury: This contract was deployed before the stored treasury and has no treasury(). Its withdrawal still takes a destination, so it can only be called from a terminal — that is the state GHO-40 is about, and it clears on the next deploy.
fees.overAccrued: More than has accrued. The contract would refuse this.

claimAll.pullBased: Winnings wait in the contract until they are collected. Any debt on the position is settled first; the rest reaches your wallet.
